title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel A, for all damping strengths gamma and stationary populations nu, has chi(A^{(x)n}) = n chi(A), with chi(A) an explicit one-variable maximum attained by two equiprobable pure states with opposite phases; and that A is additive with every finite-dimensional partner channel N for the Holevo information, the minimum output entropy and the regularized Holevo information. With the classical coding theorem, kept as the named hypothesis (CT), the classical capacity of A is chi(A) and C(A (x) N) = C(A) + C(N). The first lesson treats channels, Kraus representations, entropy, Holevo information, codes and the channel. The second writes entropy differences as integrals of log-determinants and proves a joint convexity and the concavity of a scalar deficit, each in two ways. The third proves an entropy inequality for block matrices with one zero block and extends it to the thermal block structure by a mixture with a common scalar term. The fourth bounds the output entropy of n uses by the input populations at each site and computes the Holevo information of n uses. The fifth proves additivity with an arbitrary partner and works out ordinary damping, the symmetry nu <-> 1 - nu, the unital channel and the endpoints.
prerequisites: course Entropy of automorphisms, lesson Operator convex functions and the continuity of entropy: Shannon's inequalities (Proposition 4.1) and the Fannes-Audenaert inequality (Theorem 7.1)
linear algebra: the spectral theorem, singular value decompositions, determinants and Schur complements, Hilbert-Schmidt norms
named hypothesis (CT), the classical coding theorem of Holevo and of Schumacher and Westmoreland, stated in the first lesson; not proved in the programme

checks.reading: The manuscript 'Classical capacity and entropy inequalities for generalized amplitude damping' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; paper.tex and seven section files, about 1,400 lines of TeX) was read in full on 14 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: the integral formula for entropy differences; the joint convexity of the log-determinant of a Schur complement by a contraction and by a sum of squares; the homogeneity, concavity and superadditivity of the scalar deficit, also through the Hessian determinant; the derivatives of g and the convexity of s -> g(s^2); the zero-block inequality by the Schur complement, sign averaging and zero padding; the thermal block inequality by a two-point mixture with a common scalar term and its cases u = 0; the Kraus operators of the channel, the output determinant and its completed square; the convexity of e; the branch lemma for an arbitrary partner; the site-by-site bound for pure and mixed inputs; the Holevo bound and its attainment; additivity with a partner for the Holevo information, the minimum output entropy and the regularized Holevo information; ordinary damping, the symmetry nu <-> 1 - nu, the unital midpoint and the endpoints. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the Kraus representation of a channel (Choi's argument), the diagonal bound, concavity and subadditivity in a product basis, the identity of maximal-error and average-error capacities and the existence of the regularized limit are proved in the first lesson; the completed square of the output determinant is derived from its leading coefficient, value and derivative at p = nu; the equality of the capacities of nu and 1 - nu is shown by conjugating codes, without the coding theorem. Free sources read on 14 Oct 2026: Holevo, quant-ph/9611023 (the coding theorem for a finite ensemble, read in full); Wilde, arXiv:1106.1445v8, Theorem 20.3.1 with Sections 20.3.1 and 20.3.2 (statement and error criterion checked); Tang-Zhu-Bai-Wang, arXiv:2609.28592 (Theorem 4.2, Lemma A.1, Theorem 5.5 and Corollary 6.2 read, with their numbers computed from the source); Giovannetti-Fazio, quant-ph/0405110, Section III A (the one-use maximum for ordinary damping checked against the lessons); Hastings, arXiv:0809.3972 (abstract). Checked by the program plan/checks_20261014/gad_check.py (ten parts: the integral formula on random matrices; joint convexity by midpoint tests and the sum-of-squares second derivative against finite differences; homogeneity, the integral formula, concavity and superadditivity of the scalar deficit, the derivatives of g and the Hessian determinant in 40-digit arithmetic; the zero-block and thermal inequalities on 600 random rectangular cases each, the mixture table symbolically and the sharp case; the Kraus operators and the output determinant symbolically; the branch lemma with random partners, the site bound on three qubits for pure and mixed inputs; the two-use Holevo bound against 1,200 random ensembles and its attainment; the partner chain on 200 random cases; the special cases). A first run was stopped in a slow symbolic step, which was replaced by evaluation in 40-digit arithmetic (no output kept); the next two runs failed because of errors in the check itself (random partner channels of too small Kraus rank in run a; a grid test that omitted the minimizer in run b); after the corrections all ten parts pass (run c, output gad_check_run_20261014c.txt).

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (CT): for every channel N between finite-dimensional spaces, the classical capacity is sup_n chi(N^{(x)n})/n. The direct part is Holevo's coding theorem for a fixed finite ensemble (quant-ph/9611023), applied to blocks of inputs; the converse is Holevo's entropy bound with Fano's inequality; both are proved in Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, arXiv:1106.1445v8, Theorem 20.3.1 and Sections 20.3.1-20.3.2. Not proved in the programme; it enters only through Corollary 4.2 of the fourth lesson and Theorem 3.1 of the fifth, which turn statements about Holevo information into statements about capacity. Every statement about chi and S_min is proved without it. A foundation course on quantum Shannon theory (monotonicity of relative entropy, the Holevo bound, typical subspaces and the coding theorem) would discharge it.

The programme results used from the lesson Operator convex functions and the continuity of entropy (Shannon's inequalities, the Fannes-Audenaert inequality) are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course.
The context quoted in the first lesson (Hastings's counterexample to additivity) is cited from the abstract and not used.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
